page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-standard-4 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, providing 2 threads per core. The instance is equipped with 16 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced allocation of 4 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or integrated GPU hardware.

Performance benchmarks reveal a strong single-core CPU capability, with stress-ng single-core performance scoring in the top 25%. However, multi-core scaling is relatively weak, with stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and PassMark CPU scores falling into the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth for large uncached blocks and single-threaded compression tasks perform in the average range, whereas cached small-block memory reads and multi-threaded decompression are weaker. Database operations, Redis SET throughput, and static web serving benchmarks also place in the lower tier.

From a resource density perspective, the instance offers a standard dedicated hardware profile without the overhead of shared-core burstable models, making it a predictable option for workloads that do not require massive parallel processing. Given the strong single-core performance paired with weaker multi-core and database throughput, this server is suited for single-threaded applications, basic web serving, lightweight text processing, and small-scale development environments rather than heavy database hosting or highly parallelized compute tasks.
